title: Dimension threshold for Johnson–Lindenstrauss embeddings
statement: Fix a distortion parameter $\varepsilon$ with $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and an integer $n \ge 2$. Then there is a threshold $k_0 \in \bbn$ such that for every target dimension $k \ge k_0$, every source dimension $d$, and every finite set $V \subseteq \bbr^d$ of at most $n$ points, there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$: that is, $(1-\varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2 \le \|f(u) - f(v)\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2$ for all $u, v \in V$.
hypotheses_covered: threshold k₀ holds for every target dimension k ≥ k₀
universal over every source dimension d
V finite with at most n points: |V| ≤ n
replaced:
Sub-Gaussian (Rademacher) analogue of \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_dim\_bound}:
same threshold $k_0 = O(\log n / \varepsilon^2)$, same universal conclusion for
all $k \ge k_0$, $d$, and $V$ of size at most $n$, but inheriting the
Hanson-Wright axiom from the sub-Gaussian concentration chain.
